analysis: The only change in this PR is to docs/architecture/inference.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date on line 3 and adds a new section, 'GPT-OSS decode command buffers', at head lines 4816-4826. The section says GPT-OSS plain decode steps commit a Metal command buffer every 100 operations with no input-size bound (GPTOSSDecodeCommandBuffers, via CBv2DecodeCommandBufferLimitsProviding). It also says this affects scheduling only: results do not depend on the partitioning, and prefill keeps MLX's defaults. No source code is changed in the supplied evidence, and the base text I reviewed (lines 4495-5336) contains nothing that the head text contradicts. I checked the change against the threat model. It does not touch the coordinator-provider WebSocket, attestation, App Attest authorization, key custody, prefix-cache storage (T-041), the add-on hold socket (TB-012), or the installer (TB-013). The new documentation makes no claim of changed qualification, serving grants, or secrecy. Security-relevant caveat: the actual Swift change (GPTOSSDecodeCommandBuffers) is not in the supplied evidence. Its availability or in-flight command-buffer effects (T-029, T-010) and its memory or latency behavior could not be reviewed. Whether the documentation matches that code is unverified. Nothing here supports a finding, and no threat-model update is needed from this documentation change alone.
